visualReview.notes: Reviewed the Cibali side entrance and stairs, warm brick and dressed trim, repeated arched bays, roof hips and lower west extension. Inspected corrected reveals and sills after removing light gaps in the first render.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Reviewed four directions, four architecture cameras and the overhead placement. Brick, limestone, sandstone, terracotta tile, glazing and metal remain legible. The geographic viewer fixture unloaded cleanly.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 25 current medium-fi renders. The exact mapped shell, main pitched roof, lower western mass, window rhythm and entry remain legible at all four levels. Near views show the revised arch reveals, sill shadows, canopy and railings.

geographicReview.notes: The unnamed C Block building way was selected because it contains the Qualla coordinate and faces the Cibali tram stop as specified by the museum. The university directory independently assigns the museum to C Block. The named native POI is retained as an identity reference farther northwest. I inspected the independently preserved terrain without cutout. The geographic capture used a flat viewer fixture. Placement and floor contact are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The adapted C Block factory wing that houses the Rezan Has Museum at the Cibali tram-side approach in Istanbul. The model represents the street-visible historic host building and its museum entrance.
fidelityReview.notes: University documentation of factory red brick, tall arched windows and the reused lower level guides the exterior. The primary restoration study corroborates retention of the mass and façade character. Roof subdivisions, floor heights, exact geometry of the tram-side doorway and masonry detailing are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Started with the identical photographer-released CC0 Qualla original with the historic masonry arch in the lower museum. That view guides masonry character. The standing street exterior uses the independently mapped building and institutional written evidence. No attribution-only or unconfirmed photographs were used.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Current exterior of the former Cibali Tobacco Factory’s C Block wing and the visitor approach to the Rezan Has Museum opposite Cibali station.

limitations: This is the street-visible C Block host wing of the former Cibali Tobacco Factory. The separate university wings and the enclosed subsurface cistern remain beyond its exterior scope.

The unnamed footprint is attributed to C Block by the university building directory, museum’s tram-side entrance description and the Qualla location inside the native polygon. The OSM museum point farther northwest serves as an identity reference. The exact doorway position is estimated.

The restored masonry and arched industrial openings follow the university’s account. Storey heights and counts, the exact bay rhythm, roof hips, connector glazing, lintels and color differences are reconstructions.
The unchanged Terrarium field sets the street-side approach and local slope. The stair, masonry base and side contacts are approximate.
